title: 50 Most Asked API Interview Questions
summary: Fifty interview questions for backend/SDE roles, grouped into ten themed pages. They run from REST, HTTP and status codes through auth, CORS, pagination, rate limiting, caching, gateways, webhooks, versioning and testing, to monitoring, scalability and real-world API design scenarios.

chapters.title: REST and HTTP Fundamentals
points: What is a REST API and what are its core constraints?
What is the difference between REST and SOAP?
What does it mean that HTTP is stateless, and how do you manage state anyway?
What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?
What is the difference between REST and GraphQL?

chapters.title: HTTP Methods and Status Codes
points: What is the difference between safe and idempotent HTTP methods?
What is the difference between 401 Unauthorized and 403 Forbidden?
When do you return 200, 201, 202 and 204?
What is the difference between 400, 404, 409 and 422?
What is the difference between 301, 302, 307 and 308 redirects?

chapters.title: Authentication: JWT and OAuth 2.0
points: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
How does a JWT work and what are its three parts?
What is the difference between access tokens and refresh tokens?
How does the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE work?
What is the difference between session-based and token-based authentication?

chapters.title: CORS and API Security
points: What is CORS and why does the browser block cross-origin requests?
What is a CORS preflight request and when is it triggered?
How do you protect an API against the OWASP API Top 10 risks such as BOLA?
What is the difference between API keys, OAuth and mTLS for securing APIs?
How do you prevent SQL injection, XSS and CSRF in an API?

chapters.title: Pagination, Filtering and Rate Limiting
points: What is the difference between offset pagination and cursor pagination?
Why does offset pagination get slow and inconsistent on large datasets?
How do you design filtering, sorting and field selection in a REST API?
How do the token bucket and sliding window rate limiting algorithms work?
How do you tell clients they are rate limited (429, Retry-After, RateLimit headers)?

chapters.title: Caching and Performance
points: How does HTTP caching work with Cache-Control, ETag and Last-Modified?
What is the difference between no-cache and no-store?
How do conditional requests and 304 Not Modified save bandwidth?
What is the difference between client-side, CDN and server-side (Redis) caching?
How do you invalidate a cache and what is the cache stampede problem?

chapters.title: API Gateway, Webhooks and Idempotency
points: What is an API gateway and what responsibilities does it handle?
What is the difference between an API gateway and a load balancer?
What is the difference between webhooks and polling?
How do you make a POST endpoint idempotent with an Idempotency-Key?
How do you secure and reliably deliver webhooks (signatures, retries, dedup)?

chapters.title: Versioning, File Uploads and Testing
points: What are the API versioning strategies and their trade-offs (URL, header, query)?
How do you make backward-compatible changes and deprecate an old API version?
How do you handle large file uploads (multipart, chunked, presigned URLs)?
What is the difference between unit, integration and contract tests for an API?
How do you test an API with mocks, Postman or automated CI checks?

chapters.title: Monitoring, Reliability and Scalability
points: What metrics should you monitor for an API (latency percentiles, error rate, saturation)?
What is the difference between logging, metrics and distributed tracing?
How do timeouts, retries with exponential backoff and circuit breakers work together?
How do you scale an API horizontally and why must it be stateless?
What is the difference between synchronous APIs and asynchronous queue-based processing?

chapters.title: Real-World API Design Scenarios
points: How would you design a URL shortener API?
How would you design a payment API that never charges a customer twice?
How would you design a public rate-limited API with API keys and usage tiers?
How would you design a long-running job API such as video processing or report export?
How would you design a notification API that sends to millions of users reliably?
